children: Our Bureau New Delhi: The road transport ministry Monday approved E100 or pure ethanol, along with E85, for flex-fuel vehicles, intensifying efforts to further reduce costly fuel imports. In a notification, the ministry said E85 or E100 will be used only in vehicles marked by automakers as flex-fuel. Existing vehicles cannot be tweaked to run on higher blend ethanol fuel beyond E20-a mix of 20% ethanol and 80% petrol.

The government's move comes during a period of volatility in global oil markets due to the West Asia crisis, inflating India's crude import bill. The ministry also changed certain vehicle classification thresholds, fuel specifications, and technical references used in emission-related tables and testing provisions.

This includes raising the vehicle weight limit to 3,500 kg from the previous threshold of 3,000 kg for light petrol and diesel vehicles affected by these changes. This June, Maruti Suzuki launched India's first flex-fuel car, the Wagon R Flex Fuel, capable of running on ethanol-petrol blends from E20 to E100.

title: E100 Gets Approval for Flex-Fuel Vehicle Usage
